title: Austin Budget Approvals and Staffing Changes
summary:
• **Major budget allocations approved**: The city council passed ordinances allocating $25,000 for the Water & Light Department, $10,000 for general city funds, and $2,500 for street improvements to pay approved accounts.

• **Tax revenue redistribution**: Council adjusted how property tax revenue would be divided, setting aside dedicated percentages for cemetery maintenance (2.5%), public parks (5%), and additional street improvements (2.5%).

• **City health officer appointed**: Dr. Lois H. Kirk was confirmed as the new City Health Officer by council vote.

• **Assistant city attorney resigned**: Kyrie Thrasher submitted his resignation effective immediately; the council accepted it without opposition.

• **Street lighting and pound fee disputes under review**: Citizens petitioned to maintain Congress Avenue street lights, while several residents requested refunds for impounding fees and water charges—these matters were referred to councilmen for investigation.

Austin, Texas, Jany 3rd 1910
To the Mayor and Board of Councilmen ,
City of Austin, Texas.
Gentlemen :
I hereby tender you my resignation as Assistant City Attorney of the City of Austin,
Texas, to take effect immediately.
I regret that I have to sever our relations, both officially and personally, but my own
interest demands it .
Assuring you that I am deeply grateful for confidence shown in me and kindness shown me, I
am,
Yours very respectfully.
Kyrie Thrasher.
